chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali Majiluyah (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Ubaydullah ibn Abdullah al-Dahqan, from al-Darast, from Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him) who said:

The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: "Five [groups] are to be avoided under all circumstances: the leper, the vitiligo patient, the insane, the illegitimate child, and the Bedouin."

key_terms.الْأَبْرَصُ: The vitiligo patient (one suffering from vitiligo)
key_terms.الْأَعْرَابِيُّ: The Bedouin (desert Arab, often implying distinct tribal customs)
key_terms.الْمَجْنُونُ: The insane (one suffering from mental illness)

ai.seo_question: Who are the five groups of people that should be avoided according to this hadith?
ai.summary: In *Al-Khisal*, Shaykh al-Saduq records this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) to highlight five categories of people to be avoided in all circumstances, reflecting both physical/mental conditions and social traits. While 'Al-Arabi' (Bedouin) is often interpreted as referring to those lacking refined manners or religious depth, the inclusion of 'Walad al-Zina' (child of fornication) underscores the importance of lineage and social standing in early Islamic society. This classification serves as a practical guide for social interaction and community cohesion within the Shia scholarly tradition.
